newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Six million Argentines underemployed - report.
newsitem.headline: Six million Argentines underemployed - report.

text.p: Over 6 million Argentines, or nearly 45 percent of the workforce, are unemployed or underemployed, according to a report by a private consultant published in the Clarin newspaper Wednesday.

Only 55.1 percent of the 14-million strong workforce are fully employed, according to the study by economist Luisa Montuschi. Another 15.6 percent are unemployed, 19.9 percent scrape by in underproductive jobs which do not bring in a living wage, and 9.4 percent work less than 35 hours a week but would prefer to work more.
Montuschi said unemployment had risen from 9.4 percent in 1994, but some of the rise had been offset by a fall in the percentage of workers in very badly paying jobs.
In 1994, 23.2 percent of workers had underproductive jobs, while 7.8 percent worked fewer hours than they would have liked.
